title: Madnans / Madnank
summary: Madnans or Madnank carries an uncertain Great Neck place-name history, with a possible hilly-place interpretation in older records.
address_label: General Great Neck peninsula, North Hempstead, New York
map_geometry_source: Approximate/general point for the modern Great Neck peninsula in North Hempstead; not an exact historical boundary.
introduction_content: Madnans, also written Madnank, is the history for Great Neck in North Hempstead. Early forms appear in colonial records and later histories, while the origin of the name remains uncertain.
translation_content:
The history gives two possibilities. The name may not be Indigenous at all, or, if it is Algonquian, it may contain elements for hill and land or place, giving a possible sense of a hilly place. That uncertainty should remain visible in how the name is interpreted.

Why Place Names Matter

“Indigenous place names, we argue, are expressions of Indigenous law and sovereignty, and can be used as a corrective tool if relations are imbalanced and history is recorded incorrectly.”

— Christina Gray and Andrew Ambers, The Rematriation of Indigenous Place Names (2026), Printed p. 5; PDF page 5
land_loss_content: Madnans shows how a familiar modern place can carry layered and contested origin stories. Recording Tooker's uncertainty helps avoid turning folklore or fragmentary colonial spellings into a false certainty while still preserving the placename evidence.
whereintheworld_content: The map placement is a general point for the Great Neck peninsula in North Hempstead. It orients the placename and does not define the boundaries of the historical neck.
